parts.t: One guide for each Abbotsford area I have written up so far, from city neighbourhoods to farmland. Each one covers schools, parks, planning and what to check before you buy, with a source next to every fact.
Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty. Updated October 12, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years.
Abbotsford had 153,520 people in the 2021 Census. The guides follow MLS® sub-area names, which are not City boundaries.

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Abbotsford Neighbourhood Guides

parts.t: Which Abbotsford areas have a guide?

Nine. City neighbourhoods: Abbotsford West, Central Abbotsford, Abbotsford East and Poplar. Farmland and rural areas: Aberdeen, Bradner, Matsqui, Sumas Prairie and Sumas Mountain. Each one follows its MLS® sub-area name.
Do these areas have official boundaries?
Most are MLS® sub-area names, not City of Abbotsford boundaries.

About 72% of Abbotsford’s land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and most of Aberdeen, Bradner, Matsqui and Sumas Prairie is farmland. ALR status is set property by property, so check the exact address on the

Where do I check zoning and Official Community Plan rules in Abbotsford?

The City of Abbotsford’s Zoning Bylaw and Official Community Plan set permitted uses, secondary suite rules, and subdivision minimums outside the ALR. You can check any lot on the City of Abbotsford’s interactive web map or call or text me at 604-928-1361.
